Context

The template class ara::core::BasicString provides a dynamically modifiable string in the AUTOSAR module core. The specification defines the type as an implementation of the concept std::pmr::basic_string from the ISO C++ standard [basic.string]. The fundamental design feature is the decoupling of data management and memory allocation strategy via the template parameter Allocator, which is exposed via the type alias allocator_type [SWS_CORE_03005]. The default value of the template parameter in an AUTOSAR Adaptive runtime environment likely refers to a polymorphic allocator.

Essential interaction partners of BasicString, in addition to the assigned allocator, are primarily the non-owning string view ara::core::StringView and the calling application component. Via conversion operators such as operator StringView() [SWS_CORE_03301] and corresponding constructors [SWS_CORE_03302], seamless data exchange without unnecessary dynamic memory allocations is enabled.

Context diagram: Integration of ara::core::BasicString between application, allocator, and StringView. Sources: [SWS_CORE_03005], [SWS_CORE_03301], [SWS_CORE_03302], [SWS_CORE_03415].

Lifecycle

The lifecycle of an instance of BasicString comprises creation, buffer management, state modification, and deallocation:

  • Creation and allocator binding: Instantiation is carried out via the default constructor [SWS_CORE_03024] or explicitly by passing an allocator instance [SWS_CORE_03025]. Additional overloads allow initialization from C strings [SWS_CORE_03028], StringView [SWS_CORE_03302], or iterator ranges [SWS_CORE_03031]. The assigned allocator can be queried via get_allocator() [SWS_CORE_03415].
  • Ownership and move semantics: In addition to the copy constructor [SWS_CORE_03020], the class has a default move constructor [SWS_CORE_03022] as well as a variant with allocator binding [SWS_CORE_03034]. For the move assignment operator [SWS_CORE_03023] and for swap() [SWS_CORE_03412], the exception and noexcept guarantee depends on whether allocators are equal or are propagated during move/swap operations (propagate_on_container_move_assignment and is_always_equal, respectively).
  • Destruction: At the end of the lifetime, the destructor ~BasicString() [SWS_CORE_03038] releases the allocated memory via the bound allocator.
  • Concurrency: Individual instances presumably offer no built-in protection against concurrent write accesses; concurrent modifications require synchronization on the application side.

Usage Path

A typical usage path comprises instantiation with defined allocator binding, preparatory capacity reservation, incremental modifications, and handover-ready provision:

  1. Initialization: Creation of the string object with or without allocator argument [SWS_CORE_03025].
  2. Capacity planning: Advance reservation of memory space via reserve() [SWS_CORE_03054] to avoid reallocations during frequent write operations.
  3. Composition: Appending content via append() ([SWS_CORE_03076], [SWS_CORE_03308]), operator+= ([SWS_CORE_03072], [SWS_CORE_03307]), push_back() [SWS_CORE_03083], or insert() [SWS_CORE_03310].
  4. Inspection and forwarding: Querying the dimensions via size() [SWS_CORE_03052] or empty() [SWS_CORE_03051], accessing the raw data buffer via c_str() [SWS_CORE_03069] / data() [SWS_CORE_03070], or converting into a non-owning view via operator StringView() [SWS_CORE_03301].
  5. Cleanup: Clearing the content via clear() [SWS_CORE_03057] or releasing unused capacity via shrink_to_fit() [SWS_CORE_03056].

Sequence diagram: Typical call sequence of initialization, capacity reservation, concatenation, and export as StringView. Sources: [SWS_CORE_03025], [SWS_CORE_03054], [SWS_CORE_03076], [SWS_CORE_03301].

Error Scenarios

A key deviation of ara::core::BasicString from the ISO C++ standard concerns the behavior in error conditions: Instead of standard C++ exceptions, AUTOSAR defines dedicated violations:

  • Out of range violations (IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation): Occurs instead of std::out_of_range. Is triggered when indices are outside the valid range, for example during indexed access via at(pos) with pos >= size() ([SWS_CORE_03063], [SWS_CORE_03064]), when creating substrings with substr(pos) for pos > size() [SWS_CORE_03345], for erase(pos) [SWS_CORE_03102], copy(..., pos) [SWS_CORE_03410], as well as for the corresponding overloads of insert() ([SWS_CORE_03094], [SWS_CORE_03095], [SWS_CORE_03311]), append() ([SWS_CORE_03077], [SWS_CORE_03309]), assign() ([SWS_CORE_03086], [SWS_CORE_03306]), and replace() ([SWS_CORE_03107], [SWS_CORE_03108], [SWS_CORE_03313]).
  • Length restrictions (IsoStdLengthErrorViolation): Occurs instead of std::length_error. Is caused when a size requirement exceeds the permissible maximum max_size() [SWS_CORE_03053], among others in reserve(res_arg) [SWS_CORE_03054], resize(sz) ([SWS_CORE_03058], [SWS_CORE_03059]), append() [SWS_CORE_03078], assign() [SWS_CORE_03088], insert() [SWS_CORE_03095], and replace() [SWS_CORE_03108].
  • Unchecked direct access: In accordance with the ISO C++ specification, the subscript operator operator[] ([SWS_CORE_03061], [SWS_CORE_03062]) does not perform any bounds checking. Exceeding the bounds leads to undefined behavior. For checked accesses, at() is to be preferred.

This guide is based exclusively on the specification requirements of AUTOSAR Adaptive R25-11.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  BasicString & insert (size_type pos, const value_type *s, size_type n);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [basic.string] except for the following deviations: 1. charT replaced with value_type 2. if ( pos1 > size() ) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range 3. if ( size() + n > max_size() ) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std::length_error

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function insert [SWS_CORE_03311]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  template <class T> BasicString & insert (size_type pos1, const T &t, size_type pos2, size_type n=npos);
